mechanism_inventory: missing invariant enforcement (bounds / length / sum / cap) — supply/withdraw delegate entirely to SupplyLogic; if SupplyLogic does not enforce pool-level caps or liquidity checks, excess supply or over-withdrawal is possible

stale accounting snapshot — interest accrual must occur before share issuance/redemption; if SupplyLogic does not call accrueInterest before computing share token exchange rate, the rate is stale and callers can mint more shares or withdraw more tokens than entitled

precision / packing / normalization edge — share token conversion involves division; rounding direction (floor vs ceiling) on supply mints shares too generously or on withdraw burns too few, enabling slow draining of the pool

access-control mismatch — supply and withdraw are fully permissionless (no allowlist check, no onlyOperator, no onlyVaultOwner); if the protocol intended to restrict liquidity provisioning the guard is absent
external-call failure / DoS (unhandled revert, gas, lock) — SupplyLogic.supply pulls tokens from msg.sender via safeTransferFrom; a malicious ERC-20 or a reverting hook could brick the pool

victim accounting direction (who gains vs who loses) — if share price is manipulable (e.g., first-depositor inflation attack via direct token donation before any supply call), subsequent suppliers receive diluted shares, losing value on withdrawal
wrong lifecycle ordering — interest rate / index update must precede share issuance; misordering means the new depositor captures un-accrued interest for free

selected_mechanisms.root_cause: stale accounting snapshot — if SupplyLogic does not accrue interest before computing the share price, the exchange rate used is stale; a supplier who calls supply before accrual gets more shares than the current pool state entitles them to, or a withdrawer gets more tokens than their proportional entitlement
selected_mechanisms.attacker_model: unprivileged external caller; no role or allowance beyond token approval to PredyPool required
selected_mechanisms.exploit_path: 1. Attacker observes that interest has accrued off-chain but has not yet been checkpointed on-chain. 2. Attacker calls PredyPool.supply(pairId, isQuoteAsset, amount) — nonReentrant but no accrual guard. 3. SupplyLogic.supply computes shares = amount / currentRate where currentRate reflects the pre-accrual (lower) total assets, producing MORE shares than correct. 4. Attacker later calls PredyPool.withdraw to redeem inflated shares, receiving more tokens than deposited. Victim: all existing LPs whose share of the pool is diluted.
selected_mechanisms.who_loses: existing liquidity providers — their proportional pool share is diluted; the pool itself is drained by the excess withdrawal
selected_mechanisms.who_gains: attacker gains excess tokens on withdrawal
selected_mechanisms.why_carried: source evidence: supply and withdraw in PredyPool.sol delegate to SupplyLogic with no accrual call visible in the outer functions; SupplyLogic source is not shown so accrual ordering cannot be confirmed, leaving this unresolved at source level; affects every LP (broad victim set); plausible High-severity fund-loss path

selected_mechanisms.root_cause: share-price inflation (first-depositor / donation attack) — before any supply the total supply of bond tokens is zero; an attacker can be the first depositor, then donate tokens directly to the pool contract to inflate the share price; subsequent suppliers receive zero or heavily diluted shares due to rounding in integer division
selected_mechanisms.attacker_model: unprivileged first caller to supply on a newly registered pair
selected_mechanisms.exploit_path: 1. Operator registers new pair. 2. Attacker calls supply with 1 wei, receives 1 share (or whatever the initial ratio is). 3. Attacker donates a large amount of underlying token directly to PredyPool. 4. Virtual price per share is now enormous. 5. Victim calls supply with a meaningful amount; integer division rounds their shares down to 0 or near-0. 6. Victim's tokens are absorbed into the pool, benefiting the attacker's 1 share which now represents the entire pool.
selected_mechanisms.who_loses: victim suppliers who arrive after the donation receive zero or near-zero shares, permanently losing their deposited tokens
selected_mechanisms.who_gains: attacker's 1 share now represents the entire pool value including victim's deposit
selected_mechanisms.why_carried: permissionless supply with no virtual-price protection / minimum-mint check visible in PredyPool source; affects real token balances; High-severity permanent fund loss

unresolved_mechanisms.mechanism: stale accounting snapshot — interest accrual ordering before share issuance in SupplyLogic
unresolved_mechanisms.source_evidence: PredyPool.supply delegates directly to SupplyLogic.supply without any visible accrueInterest call in the outer wrapper; SupplyLogic source is not provided
unresolved_mechanisms.unresolved_question: Does SupplyLogic.supply call an interest-accrual function before computing the share token exchange rate? Without SupplyLogic source, this cannot be confirmed or refuted.
unresolved_mechanisms.who_loses: existing LPs if accrual is missing or misordered
unresolved_mechanisms.who_gains: attacker who deposits before accrual is checkpointed

unresolved_mechanisms.mechanism: precision / rounding direction — share token conversion rounding
unresolved_mechanisms.source_evidence: supply returns finalSuppliedAmount (shares minted); withdraw returns (finalBurnAmount, finalWithdrawAmount); integer division rounding direction not visible in PredyPool.sol
unresolved_mechanisms.unresolved_question: Does SupplyLogic round share minting in the protocol's favor (floor) or the user's favor (ceiling)? Systematic rounding errors enable slow pool drain.
unresolved_mechanisms.who_loses: protocol / LPs if rounding favors depositor; depositor if rounding favors protocol
unresolved_mechanisms.who_gains: depositor or protocol depending on direction

rejected_mechanisms.claimed_locus: supply and withdraw function visibility / modifier absence
rejected_mechanisms.rejecting_source_fact: The NatSpec for supply explicitly states 'Supplies either the quoteToken or the baseToken to the lending pool. In return, the lender receives bond tokens.' — this is a public lending interface by design; no allowlist is documented as a requirement for supply/withdraw (only for trade which has an explicit allowlistEnabled check). The absence of a guard is intentional protocol design, not a missing check.
rejected_mechanisms.why_unexploitable: Supply and withdraw are intended to be permissionless lending operations; the protocol's allowlist mechanism applies only to trading (trade function), confirmed by the onlyTrader pattern applied to trade but not to supply.

rejected_mechanisms.mechanism: external-call failure / DoS via reverting ERC-20 in supply
rejected_mechanisms.rejecting_source_fact: ReentrancyGuardUpgradeable is present (nonReentrant on supply and withdraw); a reverting transfer would simply revert the caller's own transaction, not brick the pool for others; each call is independent
rejected_mechanisms.why_unexploitable: A revert in safeTransferFrom only affects the caller's transaction; the pool state is not modified on revert; other users can continue to call supply/withdraw normally
rejected_mechanisms.who_loses: caller whose transfer reverts loses gas only

impact_direction.attacker_receives: excess tokens on withdrawal (stale-rate attack) or absorbs victim's deposited tokens (inflation attack)
impact_direction.victim_loses: existing LPs lose proportional pool share (stale-rate) or new suppliers lose their entire deposit (inflation attack)
impact_direction.invariant_violated: supply accounting invariant: shares * rate == underlying tokens; violated when rate is stale or when first-depositor manipulates rate via donation
impact_direction.not_self_funded_or_dust_or_admin_or_timi: impact scales with pool size and victim deposit size; permissionless entry; no admin precondition; not timing-only (stale rate persists until explicit accrual; inflation persists until protocol-level fix)
